summary: Ep 122 ('The Legend of Kaguya. Gash's Summer Festival. The Girl Who Returned to the Moon', 2005-09-04) is an anime-original summer-festival story: Zatch goes to the festival with Hana and Ponygon, is separated, meets a rich runaway girl who calls herself Princess Kaguya, spends his last 300 yen on festival games with her, and she is collected by helicopter as 'Lady Natsuko'. Kaguya exists in no chapter (she is listed as the episode's only new character on konjikinogash.fandom and appears nowhere in the manga), and vol 20 — ch 183-192, the chapters this stretch of the anime is in — contains no festival story at all (en-WP's chapter list: 183 'Kyle's Shout', 184 'Oh My', 185 'The Awakening', 186 'A Frightening Spell', 187 'Kiyo's Mood', 188 'The Power of Riou', 189 'Faudo's True Form'). The episode's only manga-derived beat is the framing scene of Kiyomaro shut in his room researching the Demon World structure — the thread ep 121 set — which konjikinogash.fandom credits as 'Chapter 186 (Partially)' and which the same wiki's article calls out explicitly: 'While this episode features some moments originally adapted from the manga, this episode is mostly filler.' Sole-adaptation check: ch 186 'A Frightening Spell' IS the Chājiru Saifodon chapter and is adapted in full at ep 121 (konjikinogash's ep-121 field 'Chapter 185, Chapter 186'; our stored anchor ep 121 → 186 [186]), and its neighbour ch 187 'Kiyo's Mood' is adapted at ep 124 (konjikinogash ep-124 field 'Chapter 187'; our stored anchor ep 124 → 187) — so the fragment is a DUPLICATE of pages already carried by another episode, the exception cannot fire, the weight is sliver and the remainder (the entire Kaguya story) is original: ep 122 → filler, no anchor (A1).

weight: n/a (non-source) — the episode's whole plot (Zatch and the runaway 'Princess Kaguya' at the summer festival) is anime-original; Kaguya is the episode's only new character and appears in no chapter. Vol 20 (ch 183-192) carries the Momon fight, Kiyo's mood, and the opening of the Faudo arc — no festival story.
